mcq.q: Why do we collect only dead or fallen twigs?

mcq.q: In a drawing of a drum with light from the left, which part is darkest?

mcq.explanation: A chest pass begins with the ball at chest level.

mcq.explanation: Green is made from yellow and blue.

mcq.q: What do you add to a colour to make it darker?
mcq.explanation: Black makes a shade, a darker tone.

mcq.q: Overlapping in a montage means

mcq.explanation: A rest tells the performer to stay silent for a time.

mcq.q: In ta-te taa taa (rest), how many beats are there?
mcq.explanation: Each of ta-te, taa, taa and the rest fills one beat, so there are four beats.

mcq.q: Which letter has an ascender?

mcq.explanation: Ending on a crotchet, a long note, makes it sound complete.

mcq.q: How many beats does each bar have in the four-beat patterns of this lesson?
mcq.explanation: The patterns of this lesson have four beats.

mcq.q: What is the main purpose of hand signs when singing?
options: To show the pitch of the notes

mcq.q: Which move is a step?
options: m to d in one jump over r

mcq.q: Why do we knead clay before using it?
options: To make it smooth and remove air
mcq.explanation: Kneading makes clay smooth and easy to shape.

mcq.q: Before joining a coil to a slab you should
options: scratch both and dab a little water
mcq.explanation: Scratching and wetting help the clay pieces stick.

mcq.q: Why do we warm up before sprinting?
options: To prepare muscles and avoid injury
mcq.explanation: Warm muscles work better and are less likely to be hurt.

mcq.q: In a medium start, the rear knee is level with
options: the heel of the front foot
the toe of the back foot
the middle of the front foot
mcq.explanation: The medium start places the rear knee by the middle of the front foot.

mcq.q: At the set position, the hips are
options: a little higher than the shoulders
mcq.explanation: On set the hips lift slightly above the shoulders.

mcq.q: When sprinting, where should your eyes look?
mcq.explanation: Keeping the head up and eyes ahead helps balance and speed.

mcq.q: The Kenyan flag has stripes of
options: black, red and green with thin white stripes
mcq.explanation: The flag has black, red, green and white.

mcq.q: On the Kenyan flag, red stands for
options: the blood shed in the struggle for freedom
mcq.explanation: Red stands for the blood shed for freedom.

mcq.q: Why is the national flag flown at national athletics events?
options: It shows which country the athletes represent and builds pride
mcq.explanation: The flag is a symbol of the country.

mcq.q: A balance in gymnastics is
options: a position held still for a few seconds
mcq.explanation: A balance is a still position that you hold under control.

mcq.q: In a crab balance, your fingers point
mcq.explanation: In the crab position, hands are behind you with fingers pointing to the feet.

mcq.q: A side roll is also called a
mcq.explanation: Keeping the body straight like a log gives it the name log roll.

mcq.q: In which direction should a side roll travel?
options: In a curve off the mat
In a straight line along the mat
mcq.explanation: Rolling in a straight line keeps you on the mat.

mcq.q: Why do we warm up before gymnastics?
options: To prepare the muscles and joints
mcq.explanation: A warm body is less likely to be injured.

mcq.q: Which is a way to give good feedback to a partner?
options: Say one thing that was good and one thing to improve
mcq.explanation: Kind and helpful feedback includes praise and a suggestion.

mcq.q: Where should you place your hands in a crab balance?
mcq.explanation: Hands go behind you, about shoulder-width apart.

mcq.q: If you finish a gymnastics session, what should you do?
options: Put equipment away and cool down
mcq.explanation: Tidying and cooling down are good habits.

mcq.q: A song about washing hands to prevent germs is a
mcq.explanation: It gives a message about a topic of importance.

mcq.q: Dynamics means
options: how loud or soft the music is
mcq.explanation: Dynamics are the loud and soft parts.

mcq.q: A song that is played fast has a
mcq.explanation: Tempo is speed.

mcq.q: Gestures in singing are
options: hand and body movements that fit the song
mcq.explanation: Gestures help tell the story of a song.

mcq.q: Unison singing is suitable for an anthem because
options: everyone can join in the same tune
mcq.explanation: A single tune that everybody sings is simple and strong.

mcq.q: Funeral songs are usually
mcq.explanation: They comfort families and remember the person.

mcq.q: In a folk song, the singer who leads is called the
mcq.explanation: The soloist sings the lead part.

mcq.q: Which of these can also take digital photographs?
mcq.explanation: Many tablets have cameras.

mcq.q: Photos on a digital device are kept in its
mcq.explanation: Digital photos are stored in memory.

mcq.q: Who should you ask before using a school digital device?
mcq.explanation: Always get permission.

mcq.q: Which light is best for outdoor photographs?
options: Natural sunlight falling on the subject
mcq.explanation: Natural light is best.

mcq.q: Indoors, the best place to stand for better light is
options: near a window or open door
mcq.explanation: Daylight helps.

mcq.q: When photographing a child, it is good to
options: bend down to their eye level
mcq.explanation: Eye level gives a friendly picture.

mcq.q: Why delete poor photographs?
options: So memory is not filled up
mcq.explanation: Deleting saves space.

mcq.q: Another name for the descant recorder is the
mcq.explanation: The descant is the soprano recorder.

mcq.q: Which joint has the mouthpiece?
mcq.explanation: The mouthpiece is at the top of the head joint.

mcq.q: Uncovering holes makes the note
mcq.explanation: Shorter air column means a higher note.

mcq.q: Where should the mouthpiece rest?
options: Between your lips, not your teeth
mcq.explanation: Lips form the seal.

mcq.q: Why should recorders not be shared without cleaning?
options: Germs can spread through the mouthpiece
mcq.explanation: Saliva can carry disease-causing germs.

mcq.q: Which note is played with the thumb and holes 1 and 2 covered?
mcq.explanation: A uses thumb, 1 and 2.

mcq.q: How many lines are on a staff?
mcq.explanation: The staff has five lines.

mcq.q: The song Hot Cross Buns can be played on
mcq.explanation: It uses the three notes B, A and G.

mcq.q: Where should beginners stay in the pool?
mcq.explanation: Shallow water is safer.

mcq.q: Which is a safe way to enter the pool?
options: Feet first, watched by the teacher
mcq.explanation: Feet-first entry is safe.

mcq.q: Water games help learners to
mcq.explanation: They build confidence.

mcq.q: Floating means
options: staying on top of the water without swimming
mcq.explanation: Floating is resting on the surface.

mcq.q: In a supine float, you lie
options: on your back with ears in the water
mcq.explanation: You look at the sky.

mcq.q: In a glide, your face is
options: in the water with the head between your arms
mcq.explanation: Keeping the face in helps the body stay level.

mcq.q: Outside the pool, in a river or the sea, you should
options: only go in with a trusted adult who can swim
mcq.explanation: Open water is more dangerous.

mcq.q: In the frog jump, you begin
options: in a squat with your hands on the ground
mcq.explanation: You squat and spring forward.

mcq.q: The elephant walk stretches the
options: back and the back of the legs
mcq.explanation: Bending forward stretches those muscles.

mcq.q: The giraffe stretch mainly improves
mcq.explanation: Stretching increases flexibility.

mcq.q: Which Kiswahili word means snake?
mcq.explanation: Nyoka is a snake.

mcq.q: Why do animal games often use singing or drumming?
options: Rhythm helps players move together and adds fun
mcq.explanation: Music sets the pace.

mcq.q: Which is a rule for animal games?
options: Do not push, trip or pull others
mcq.explanation: Safety comes first.

mcq.q: Who can teach you an indigenous game from your community?
mcq.explanation: Elders know many traditional games.

mcq.q: Which is an example of appropriate behaviour when viewing a display?
mcq.explanation: Respect for others' work is important.

mcq.q: A working portfolio holds
options: work in progress such as sketches and trials
mcq.explanation: It shows how work develops.

mcq.q: What should be written on the portfolio label?
mcq.explanation: A label shows whose portfolio it is.

mcq.q: Every displayed work should have
options: a label with the title and artist's name
mcq.explanation: Labels help viewers.

mcq.q: Which value is found in the Kenya National Anthem?
mcq.explanation: The anthem speaks of unity, peace, justice and service.

mcq.q: Which is a component of a folk song?
mcq.explanation: Components include community, type, message, participants and instruments.

mcq.q: Sportsmanship means
options: being fair and kind in sports
mcq.explanation: It includes following rules and respecting others.

short.q: Why does a drum sound higher when its skin is tightened?
short.answer: A tighter skin vibrates faster. Faster vibration makes a higher sound. Ropes are used to tighten the skin.
short.working: 1 mark for faster vibration, 1 mark for higher sound, 1 mark for the ropes or tightening.

short.q: Describe how you would improvise a rhythm to accompany a song.
short.answer: Sing the song and find the beat by tapping. Play the beat on an instrument. Change to a pattern, such as two quick sounds and a long sound. Repeat it and change it at the end of a verse.
short.working: 1 mark for each step, up to 4.

short.q: Why should you collect only dead or fallen twigs for charcoal?
short.answer: To protect the environment and living trees. Dead twigs are also dry.
short.working: 1 mark for protecting living trees, 1 mark for the environment or dry wood.

short.q: List four steps of the medium start.
short.answer: Front foot about one and a half foot lengths behind the line; kneel on the rear knee level with the middle of the front foot; hands behind the line shoulder-width apart; on set, lift the hips a little above the shoulders.

short.q: Give three warm-up activities before sprinting.
short.answer: Jogging, arm circles, leg swings, gentle stretching, short easy strides. Any three.

short.q: How should we behave towards the national flag?
short.answer: Do not let it touch the ground, do not write on it, keep it clean and not torn, and stand still and quiet when it is raised.

short.q: Describe a full netball court.
short.answer: It is a rectangle 30.5 metres long and 15.25 metres wide. It is divided into three equal thirds. It has a goal post at each end with a goal circle and a centre circle in the middle.
short.working: 1 mark for the rectangle with measurements, 1 mark for thirds, 1 mark for circles or posts.

short.q: State four rules of netball.
short.answer: No running with the ball; pass or shoot within three seconds; no contact; defenders stand 0.9 metres away; start with a centre pass. Any four.

short.q: What does giving with the ball mean in netball catching?
short.answer: Bending the arms as the ball arrives so as to take the force out of it.
short.working: 1 mark for bending arms, 1 mark for softening the catch.

short.q: Why is colour classification important in painting?
short.answer: It helps us know which colours to mix to get others. It shows that only primary colours are needed to make all the other colours.

short.q: How do you care for a paint brush?
short.answer: Rinse when changing colour, wash with soap after use, shape the tip and store it flat or with hairs up. Never leave it standing on its hairs in water.

short.q: Give three qualities of a neat montage.
short.answer: Clean cut edges, no glue marks, well-overlapped pieces, firmly stuck and a clear title. Any three.

short.q: Explain why a pair of quavers is the same length as one crotchet.
short.answer: A quaver is half a beat. Half plus half makes one whole beat. A crotchet is one beat.

short.q: What are ascenders and descenders in lettering? Give one example of each.
short.answer: An ascender is the part of a letter that goes up above the small letters, such as b. A descender goes below the baseline, such as p.
short.working: 1 mark for each meaning, 1 mark for correct examples.

short.q: Describe how to critique a friend's rhythmic pattern with respect.
short.answer: Say one good thing first. Talk about the steadiness of the beat, variation and the ending. Give one suggestion to make it better. Listen to others' views politely.

short.q: State three qualities of a good melody.
short.answer: Stepwise motion, variation of syllables and note lengths, and ending on d.

short.q: State the recorder notes that match d, r and m.
short.answer: If G is doh, then G, A and B match d, r and m. G is d, A is r and B is m.

short.q: How can you show that you have identified the pitch of a note by ear?
short.answer: Listen to the note, decide if it is low, middle or high, and make the hand sign for it.
short.working: 1 mark for listening, 1 mark for deciding pitch, 1 mark for hand sign.

short.q: Describe how to do the side roll safely.
short.answer: Lie on the back with body straight. Stretch the arms overhead with palms together and legs together. Tighten the tummy and point the toes. Roll over on to the side and tummy in a straight line. Get up slowly.

short.q: Give four ways in which gymnastics helps the body.
short.answer: Makes muscles stronger; improves flexibility; improves balance and coordination; exercises the heart and lungs; builds confidence. Any four.

short.q: Explain the difference between a sacred song and a patriotic song.
short.answer: A sacred song is a song of worship that praises God. A patriotic song shows love for the country, such as the national anthem.
short.working: 1 mark for each meaning, 1 mark for an example.

short.q: Give three examples of good etiquette during a performance.
short.answer: Walk on and off quietly, listen to the leader, do not talk or laugh, clap for others, bow at the end. Any three.

short.q: Why are funeral songs usually slow and sad?
short.answer: They comfort the family and remember the person who has died, so the mood is calm and serious.

short.q: State the jobs of the lens, the screen and the battery of a camera.
short.answer: The lens lets light in; the screen shows the view and photos; the battery gives power.

short.q: Why should you never point a camera directly at the sun?
short.answer: It can hurt your eyes and the strong light will spoil the picture.
short.working: 1 mark for eyes, 1 mark for picture, 1 mark for explanation.

short.q: Why should you delete poor photographs from a device?
short.answer: To save memory space, keep only good pictures and make it easier to find the best ones.

short.q: Give four hygiene measures for using a recorder.
short.answer: Wash hands before playing; do not share it without cleaning; do not eat while playing; wipe the mouthpiece; clean it properly. Any four.

short.q: Describe the fingering for B, A and G.
short.answer: B uses the thumb and hole 1; A uses the thumb and holes 1 and 2; G uses the thumb and holes 1, 2 and 3.

short.q: Why is swimming an essential life skill?
short.answer: It helps people stay safe near water and prevent drowning, and it keeps the body fit.

short.q: Why do we play water games in shallow water with the teacher?
short.answer: To feel safe and in control, to learn to breathe and move with confidence and to avoid accidents.

short.q: Give three hygiene rules for the pool.
short.answer: Shower before and after; do not spit or pass urine in the pool; do not drink the water; dry yourself and change into dry clothes. Any three.

short.q: Name two animal movement games.
short.answer: Frog jump, crab walk, elephant walk, snake slither, hare hop, crocodile crawl, giraffe stretch, monkey swing. Any two.

short.q: State four rules for playing the hawk and the chicks game.
short.answer: Hold but do not pull; the hawk tags gently; no pushing or tripping; stop at the whistle; take turns. Any four.

short.q: Why is it good to take different roles in animal games?
short.answer: Everyone gets a fair turn, learns to lead and follow, and the team works better.

short.q: State three qualities of good feedback.
short.answer: Kind, honest, specific and helpful. Any three.

short.q: Describe how to present an artwork from your portfolio.
short.answer: Hold it carefully, say the title, explain the materials and skills, tell the message, say what you like and what you would change, and listen to feedback.

short.q: List the components of a folk song that you can analyse.
short.answer: Community of origin, type or occasion, message, participants and their roles, and instruments.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four correct components.

short.q: Explain how a drum makes sound and how its parts work together.
short.answer: The beater or hand strikes the drumhead, which vibrates and makes the sound. The hollow shell makes the sound fuller and louder. The ropes hold the skin tight, and a tighter skin gives a higher sound.
short.working: 1 mark each for striking, vibrating skin, shell, ropes, and effect of tightness on pitch.

short.q: Describe a sequence that joins the crab balance and the side roll, and how to perform it safely.
short.answer: Warm up and use a mat with a clear space. Do a crab balance and hold for three counts. Lower to the mat and lie straight with arms overhead. Do a side roll in a straight line. Get up slowly and finish standing tall.
short.working: 1 mark each for safety, crab balance, lowering, roll, and finish.

short.q: Explain how to analyse a folk song performance using its components.
short.answer: Say the community of origin, the type or occasion, the message and mood, the roles of the soloist, chorus and instrumentalists, and the instruments used.
short.working: 1 mark for each of five components.
